# The Margins

The first correction appeared on a Tuesday, in a copy of *The Sea Around Us* that had been on the shelf since before Marisol became head librarian at the Point Alvarado Branch. She was flipping through it during a lull—honestly, she was procrastinating on the budget report—when she noticed the pencil marks. Faint, precise, in a small neat hand. *Tide pools are not always visible at low tide,* someone had written in the margin beside a passage, *depending on the season and the beach's slope. See p. 87 of the revised edition.*

Marisol frowned. She checked the borrowing history. The book had gone out eleven times in the past three years. The last patron was listed only as a number, per privacy rules, but the return date was four days ago.

She should have been annoyed. Writing in library books was vandalism, technically. But the correction was *right*—she looked it up, and the revised edition did say exactly that. And the pencil was so light she could have erased it without a trace. Whoever this was had been careful. Almost apologetic.
